name: Public record

subjectOf.text: Similar business deals and contracts between counterparties must be organized and reviewable by the public, and the transaction history has to be fully openly viewable and verifiable so that parties can see that counterparties will perform as expected.
subjectOf.abstract: The history of transactions has to be fully openly viewable and verifiable, so that business parties can see that their counterparties will perform as expected.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Commerce – A Primer on Why Decentralized Reputation Verification Systems Are Needed (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3405401

subjectOf.text: A functioning decentralized reputation system requires that counterparties' actions in decentralized commerce endure and become part of a public record: their actions must stick and become part of a meaningful precedence system.
subjectOf.abstract: This necessitates that counterparties' actions in decentralized commerce endure and become part of a public record. In other words, counterparties' actions need to stick. Their actions have to become part of a precedence system that is meaningful.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Commerce – A Primer on Why Decentralized Reputation Verification Systems Are Needed (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3405401

subjectOf.text: Increasing counterparty trust in decentralized commerce requires that the full history of transactions be openly viewable and verifiable, so that counterparties' actions endure as part of a public record and a meaningful precedence system.
subjectOf.abstract: The history of transactions has to be fully openly viewable and verifiable, so that business parties can see that their counterparties will perform as expected.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization - A Primer on the New Economy (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3406323
scope_conditions: decentralized smart contract based commerce between anonymous parties
